en.html:
Kageaki had left the house in the morning again. Surely he would not come back until late at night.

By now he must be wearing away his time and strength on another aimless round of the town. That work of his: chewing over the meaninglessness of his own life, then chewing it again.

景明は今日も朝から家を空けていた。
　きっと夜が更けるまで戻らないだろう。

　今頃はまた、目的もない町の巡り歩きで時間と体力
を磨り減らしているに違いない。
　己の命の無意味さを噛み締めるような、あの作業で。

en.html:
I let out a sigh as though dropping it onto the tatami. It came out much bigger and deeper than I had intended.

Nobody scolded me. I could have shouted the house down and received the same response. Very considerate house. Whatever foolishness I did, no objection. After a while I would have welcomed one objection. When Kageaki was out, I was the only one left here.

Apparently this house belonged to his father. Not once had I seen the man inside it. There had been a servant called Makimura, but for some time now she too had been away.

When had I stopped seeing that person who made so little impression? Such a simple thing to remember, no? Five hundred years inside this head, but ask it when the servant last came and suddenly it has become one empty pot. I tried. It would not come.

Since the battle with the Silver Star ended, my heartsteel had been dull somehow. Probably because the mission engraved in it—the reason for my existence—was gone.

Five hundred years. And these last two years.
Meetings, partings, battles, deaths.

Now everything seemed to have happened far away.

Was I approaching death as a tsurugi, with all my workings growing weaker?

ja.html:
畳の上へ落とすように、一つ息をつく。
　思いのほか、大きく深くなった。

　誰にも咎められはしなかったけれども。
　それは大声で喚き散らしたとしても同じだったろう。
景明がいない時、家に残るのは私一人だ。

　この家は景明の父のものだというが、ここで彼の姿
を見たことは一度もない。
　牧村という使用人がいたが――彼女もここしばらく
は他出している。

　あの存在感の薄い人をいつから見なくなったのか。
　……思い出そうとして、できなかった。簡単なこと
のはずなのに。

　銀星号との戦いが終わって以来、<ruby>心鉄<rt>こころ</rt></ruby>はどこか鈍い。
　おそらく――そこに刻まれた使命、存在理由が失わ
れたからだ。

　過去五百年。そしてこの二年間。
　出会いと訣別と戦いと死と。
　
　今は何もかも、遠い出来事のようだった。

　劒冑としての死が近付き、あらゆる働きが衰えつつ
あるのか。

en.html:
Except that one part of my heartsteel would not follow the rest.

There was something that did not grow distant at all. The duller I became as a tsurugi, the more a feeling from the time when I had a flesh-and-blood body woke somewhere inside me. That part kept one person close. Very close.

それは心鉄の一部分を除いてのこと。

　ちっとも遠くならないものがある。
　劒冑として鈍磨するのに反比例して、肉体を持って
いた頃の感性がどこかで目覚めて、その部分が一つの
ものを近く強く想っている。

en.html:
Kageaki.

...My pilot.

He was not a tsurugi, heading toward death when its reason to exist was gone. Even without a reason to live, his heart would beat, his blood would circulate. Living had to continue, just as before.

While shame and regret burned him from inside.

ja.html:
景明。

　……私の<ruby>仕手<rt>つかいて</rt></ruby>。

　彼は存在理由を失えば死に向かう劒冑とは違う。
　例え生きる理由を失っても、心臓は動き血液は巡り、
何も変わらず生き続けなくてはならない。

　慙愧と悔恨に身中を灼かれながら。

en.html:
This was not the ending I had wanted.
I was glad he had survived. Of course I was. But surviving just so he could suffer—this was not what I had wished for him.

Should I be grateful at least that he showed no sign of impulsively taking his own life? But the reason was that he would not allow himself any escape.

Throw everything away and find relief: that way, he could not choose.

I could not bear to have him die.
But if he stayed like this... what difference would remain?

If all his anguish kept collecting inside, with no way to let it out, sooner or later it would eat through him. Body dead or heart dead. Only that difference.

ja.html:
こんな結末を望んではいなかった。
　生き残ってくれたのは嬉しい。けれど苦しむために
生き延びて欲しかったのではなかった。

　衝動的に自殺する様子が見えないだけ、良かったと
思うべきなのだろうか。
　しかし彼がそうしないのは、自分自身に逃避を許さ
ないからなのだ。

　何もかも投げ捨てて楽になるという道を選べない。

　死んでしまわれては困る。
　でも、このままでは――――同じだ。

　懊悩を溜め込み、逃す方法を知らなければ、いずれ
内側から腐蝕する。
　体が死ぬか心が死ぬかの違いでしかない。

en.html:
That feeling was strong.

I, Muramasa, was of no use anymore. Let me sleep. Let me crumble away. But leaving him like this—that I could not do.

ja.html:

　けれど、彼をこのままにしてはおけなかった。
